text:
The act of State doctrine holds that the courts of one country will not judge the legality of a recognized foreign sovereign’s public acts done inside that sovereign’s own territory. Courts treat those official acts as valid and leave challenges to diplomacy or the foreign state’s own legal system rather than domestic litigation. The rule is strongest in United States foreign-relations law (Underhill v. Hernandez; Banco Nacional de Cuba v. Sabbatino) and has a related, narrower form in English public law.
